part.text: {"variants":[{"id":"V1","title":"Full-capsid, membrane-anchored receptor enumeration of the 3-fold GPI engagement motif","text":"Enumerate binding modes of the full 60-mer capsid at the 3-fold spike against membrane-embedded, GPI-anchored LY6A and the rest of the BBB receptor panel (LY6C1, ALPL, LRP6, CA4, AAVR) with docking, MD refinement and AlphaFold-Multimer, rather than against the isolated VR-VIII peptide (AA587–594) used in APPRAISE-style competition modeling. Anchor the sweep on the published PHP.eB–LY6A complex (PDB 7WQO) rebuilt with its GPI anchor and a lipid-bilayer patch, and test whether transcytosis-competent pairs share a 3-fold-axis anchor geometry that non-cognate pairs lack. Published modeling covers only peptide-scale complexes, e.g. AlphaFold-Multimer models of LRP6 with AAV-X1 and CAP-Mac VR-VIII peptides (https://pmc.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/articles/PMC11381518), so whether the motif survives a whole-capsid, membrane-proximal representation is untested.","root_link":"Bears on Q3 of the root question — which capsid–receptor binding signatures permit transcytosis — by asking whether the shared 3-fold-axis GPI-engagement motif is a property of the intact capsid engaging a membrane receptor rather than of peptide competition.","compute_open":"More parallel compute buys full-capsid × receptor × pose jobs, which are far more expensive per model than peptide jobs; published measurements of depth effects stop at single-digit peptide complexes per study, and above that it is unknown whether whole-capsid sampling preserves, sharpens or dissolves the shared-motif call.","sequential":"none: every full-capsid–receptor pose is an independent docking or AlphaFold-Multimer job with its own random seeds.","changes":"Changes the system studied — full 60-mer capsid with a GPI-anchored receptor in a membrane patch at the 3-fold spike, instead of isolated AA587–594 peptides. This closes the named gap that a 'shared 3-fold motif' may partly reflect the peptide-competition setup, and it matters to the Gradinaru/APPRAISE programme, whose current pipeline is peptide-based, and to Voyager's capsid–receptor mechanism step, which reads real capsid engagement.","narrowing":"Leaves aside everything after binding — endosomal sorting, lysosomal degradation, nuclear import — so the computed interface geometry stands in only for the binding step. It still moves the root question because it decides whether the candidate signature catalog (Q3) survives when the capsid is modeled as it actually engages the receptor, which sets what Q1's sufficiency claim has to test."},{"id":"V2","title":"Motif call judged against matched human Transwell transcytosis labels on conserved ALPL","text":"Enumerate binding modes of engineered capsid libraries against the BBB receptor panel (LY6A, LY6C1, ALPL, LRP6, CA4, AAVR) with docking, MD refinement and AlphaFold-Multimer, but judge the competent-minus-retained motif gap against per-pair transcytose-versus-retain labels measured in a human polarized barrier (Transwell) assay for ALPL, the conserved panel receptor, anchored on Voyager's VCAP-102 ± ALPL versus AAV9 result. Keep the published PHP.eB–LY6A complex as the structural control for the pose rebuild, and score the motif only on pairs that carry a direct human transcytosis measurement rather than on mixed-species in vivo transduction. Published modeling covers single-digit complexes, and the only published Transwell comparison is VCAP-102/ALPL against AAV9 (https://www.voyagertherapeutics.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/05/POSTER-Voyager_ASGCT_2024_FINAL_Ishan.pdf).","root_link":"Bears on Q1 and Q3 of the root question — whether a binding signature is sufficient for transcytosis — by asking whether the 3-fold-axis GPI-engagement gap separates transcytosis-competent from retained pairs when labels come from human endothelium and a conserved receptor.","compute_open":"More parallel compute buys pose models across the expanded, label-matched ALPL pair set (72 pairs at 144, 720 and 2,880 models); previously only a single transcytosis pair existed to compare against, so whether a motif emerges once labels are measured in the same human assay is unknown.","sequential":"none: each capsid–receptor pose is an independent docking or AlphaFold-Multimer job, and the Transwell measurements are a separate bench block that does not gate the pose sweep.","changes":"Changes the comparison it is judged against — matched human Transwell transcytosis measurements built around Voyager's VCAP-102±ALPL versus AAV9 result, instead of scarce mixed-species phenotype labels. This closes the label-scarcity gap and the species gap (ALPL is conserved while LY6A/LY6C1 are mouse-restricted and 9P31/9P36 bind mouse but not primate CA4), and it targets Voyager's TRACER / ALPL NeuroShuttle mechanism-of-action step and Dyno's ALPL mechanism assignment.","narrowing":"Leaves aside post-binding fate beyond the barrier readout and any receptor without a matched transcytosis measurement, so the observable stands in for transcytosis rate across human endothelium rather than for in vivo brain transduction. It moves the root question because it converts Q1's sufficiency claim into a test on human-relevant pairs instead of mouse-restricted signatures."},{"id":"V3","title":"Motif calls emitted for Capsida NR001–NR005 and Lir Starfish binding-assay readouts","text":"Enumerate binding modes of capsid libraries against the human BBB-receptor set used by Capsida's NR001–NR005 platform and Lir's Starfish capsid-structure pipeline (ALPL, AAVR, LRP6 and their panel partners) with docking, MD refinement and AlphaFold-Multimer, emitting calls in the format of plate- and bead-based capsid–receptor binding assays. Score whether 3-fold-axis engagement geometry agrees with measured bind/no-bind receptor by receptor, then rank the binding-positive pairs as the only candidates worth a transcytosis claim. Published modeling covers only single-digit complexes, and neither Capsida's nor Lir's structural pipeline has been assessed against exhaustive enumeration.","root_link":"Bears on Q3 of the root question — which capsid–receptor binding signatures are candidates for transcytosis — by pruning the catalog to pairs that survive a real human-receptor binding assay before any transcytosis claim (Q1) is attempted.","compute_open":"More parallel compute buys model runs across capsid × receptor × pose for the NR001–NR005 receptor set, letting the shared-motif question be tested receptor by receptor against binding readouts rather than at a single receptor; published depth effects stop at single-digit complexes and the proprietary pipelines are unmeasured, so the payoff is unknown.","sequential":"none: each capsid–receptor pose is an independent docking or AlphaFold-Multimer job with its own seeds, and the plate/bead binding readouts are a separate block.","changes":"Changes the programme it is aimed at — output is scored against Capsida's NR001–NR005 human BBB-receptor platform and Lir's Starfish docking pipeline instead of against phenotype labels. This closes the named gap that these two additional consumers were not assessed and that binding-only, human-relevant receptors are exactly what their assays read.","narrowing":"Leaves aside transcytosis and all post-binding fate — the observable is binding agreement plus interface geometry, not fate. It still moves the root question by narrowing the candidate signature catalog (Q3) to pairs that survive a human-receptor binding assay, which is the precondition for any sufficiency test (Q1)."}]}
